All roadmap promises (how to read, topic index and sections, by chapter) were predicted in order. Matches the expected answer.

Post level: both readers describe the order as reading rules, then the topic map, the topic sections in identifier order, the chapter index and the closing chain, which agrees with the declared prerequisite_order with grouping for the topic sections; neither marks any section's position unclear. Reader B's B1 (only twelve topic sections) is a miscount: the draft has thirteen (economics, six company sections, six technical topics), as reader A confirmed.

results.quote: The research briefs mentioned in the opening are left out: the chapters rely on these briefs, written in October 2026 to collect and check the company, regulatory and practice facts the chapters use.
results.finding: After the colon the reader expects the reason the briefs are left out and gets why they matter; the reason ('working notes, not public evidence') comes a sentence later. Reader A: 'I had to re-read to see that the clause after the colon describes the briefs and does not justify leaving them out.' Reader B: 'I read it twice to see whether "these briefs" were the excluded ones or the cited ones.' The spec's controlling idea is fine; the sentence order inside the paragraph obscures it.

results.quote: two links count as one source when they differ only in scheme, `www.`, a trailing slash, a fragment, an `.html` suffix or an arXiv version
results.finding: Identifier and deduplication mechanics come before the reader knows what an entry looks like (How to Read ¶3) or what the topics are ('Identifiers were assigned in topic order' before the Topic Index). Reader A: 'the dedup rules are hard to picture until you know what an entry looks like'; reader B: 'I had to hold "topic order" without knowing what it referred to.' Both propose putting the entry anatomy (p05) first. Both rate the cost small. The difficulty comes from the spec's order p03-p04-p05; the draft's detailed normalization list and the forward reference to topic order add to it.

results.quote: because the topic list the identifiers were assigned from put them in that order
results.finding: The reason given for Platform preceding Web is circular; both readers re-read it looking for a real reason. Reader A: 'This reason is circular'; reader B: 'It says the order is X because the list was in order X.' The following sentence ('The order was fixed when the identifiers were assigned and does not change') carries the real reason; the parenthetical can be cut or reduced to it.

results.quote: The toolkit presents each template as the smallest form that makes a decision explicit, assigns an owner and leaves evidence someone else can check.
results.finding: The sentence breaks the description of the chain to describe the toolkit's design; its point appears only with the next sentence. Reader A: 'I had to read on to see its point'; reader B: 'understandable but indirect.' The callback is required by the spec (p34); placing or joining it so it plainly leads into 'This chain is how that check is made' is a draft fix. Both readers say they followed it.

results.finding: Reader A only (A5): the text explains why company sources are grouped but not why the company block precedes the technical topics, which come earlier in the book. Minor.

Entry-level; the general rule in How to Read (look at the year) still lets the reader judge. Uncorroborated, minor.

Other terms are given before use or are within the audience's knowledge: 'Part IX' is now glossed as the book's case-study chapters, 'The Forced Fit' is glossed in its bullet, evidence types are defined in the table.
Direct-statement hook followed by context and a roadmap; no dictionary definition, throat-clearing or generic sweep.
The conclusion neither restates the page section by section nor opens with 'In conclusion'; the closing sentence is the spec's prescribed callback to the third key point.

¶1 joins the three reference pages into one chain from template to dated source (synthesis); ¶2 tells the reader what to do before citing a source (so-what, course-of-action takeaway); ¶3 marks where the chain stops.
¶1 calls back to the toolkit's 'evidence someone else can check'; ¶3 calls back to the KEY POINTS bullet on keeping documented facts, inferences and Veldmark distinct.
